headlines: Bench Gets a Fresh Coat and a New Friendship
A Place to Sit, Thanks to Two Neighbors
bodies: {A} and {B} repainted a public bench on {street}. After disagreeing over the color, they agreed to share the first seat.
The bench on {street} is freshly painted, courtesy of {A} and {B}. The pair finished with paint on both sets of shoes and plans to meet there again.
{B} offered to help {A} paint a bench on {street}. The work ended with a handshake and a standing invitation to sit together.

headlines: Wet Paint Notice Arrives Too Late
Bench Project Ends in a Colorful Dispute
Fresh Bench Paint Spoils a Neighborly Gesture
bodies: {B} repainted a bench on {street} but neglected a wet-paint notice. {A} sat down and rose with a ruined coat and a grievance.
A freshly painted bench on {street} caught {A} by surprise. {B}, responsible for the paint and the missing warning, received a sharp public rebuke.
{A} discovered the new bench paint with the back of a coat. An argument with {B} followed, and the Gazette advises readers to inspect before sitting.

items.era_notes: Use the same wording throughout; the paint, bench and handwritten warning require no decade-specific technology.

headlines: Crooked Loaves Find a Loyal Following
Bakery Turns a Baking Mishap into a Bargain
Uneven Bread Draws an Even Longer Line
bodies: A batch of lopsided loaves at {shop} sold out after {A} offered them at a discount. Customers said the bread tasted better than it stood.
{A} labeled a crooked batch of bread 'leaning loaves' and lowered the price. The last one left {shop} before noon.
An uneven rise made this morning's bread at {shop} difficult to stack. {A} sold every loaf at a reduced price and took requests for another batch.

headlines: Bakery Refunds a Morning's Worth of Bread
Salt Mix-Up Brings Refunds at the Bakery
Baker Owns Up to an Unfortunate Batch
bodies: {A} discovered too much salt in a batch at {shop} and refunded every buyer who returned. The mistake cost a morning's receipts but earned thanks for the warning.
Customers at {shop} received an apology and their money back after an oversalted batch. {A} posted a notice before anyone had to ask.
A measuring error spoiled the morning bread at {shop}. {A} offered refunds and accepted the resulting jokes with visible effort.

items.era_notes: Keep notices on paper and transactions in unspecified currency. The story assumes A owns the bakery bound to shop.

items.text: They say {A} anonymously paid for the new hymnbooks at the church.
variants: I hear {A} paid for those hymnbooks; some people save up to do a kindness.
New hymnbooks, anonymous donor; people say it was {A}.
If {A} bought the hymnbooks, who let the secret slip, and why now?

items.text: Word is {A} has been moving the boundary stakes to steal a strip of land from {B}.
variants: I hope that talk about {A} shifting stakes on {B} is a misunderstanding.
They say {A} moved the stakes against {B}; get the land measured.
Funny how that boundary supposedly creeps toward {B} whenever {A} has a shovel out.

items.text: I hear {A} deliberately misspelled the last word in the spelling contest so another child could win.
variants: They say {A} gave away that spelling prize; I hope nobody makes a fuss and spoils the kindness.
Supposedly {A} missed the word on purpose.
{A} spelled every harder word, then missed that one; who was the prize really meant for?

items.text: They say {A} keeps a second price list at {shop} for customers who look desperate.
variants: I hate to think {A} charges more when someone badly needs a repair, but that is the talk about {shop}.
People say desperation costs extra at {shop}, courtesy of {A}.
Has anyone compared two receipts from {shop}? They say {A} prices the customer before the nails.

items.text: People say {A} leaves an empty chair facing the river and speaks to it before dawn.
variants: They say {A} talks to an empty chair by the river; perhaps it helps with something private.
An empty chair, the river, {A} talking before sunrise; that is what I heard.
If that chair by the river is empty, why do people say {A} pauses as though someone answers?

items.text: I hear {A} entered a vegetable grown by {B} in the fair and claimed the ribbon.
variants: I hope {A} and {B} sort out whose vegetable won that ribbon before a friendship goes sour.
They say the ribbon went to {A} and the gardening was all {B}.
Did {A} grow that prize vegetable, or just carry it over from {B}? People are asking.
